title: A sharp fall in UK financial complaints partly reflects changed access to the ombudsman, not necessarily less consumer harm
source_unit: UK Financial Ombudsman Service, Annual complaints data and insight 2025/26
geography: United Kingdom; complaints referred to the Financial Ombudsman Service and Financial Ombudsman Service for Small Businesses

denominator.unit: new complaints received by the Financial Ombudsman Service in 2025/26

complaint_change_percent.unit: percent change in new complaints received

overall_uphold_rate.unit: percent of complaints resolved in consumers' favour across financial products

mechanism.value: A fall in complaints is an ambiguous consumer signal: it can reflect less harm, less referral capacity, changed redress rules, or altered willingness and ability to pursue a case

observations.method: Annual administrative complaint totals and overall uphold rate reported by the Financial Ombudsman Service for financial year 2025/26, compared with 2024/25.
observations.uncertainty: Complaint volume is a routed administrative outcome, not a population incidence rate; uphold rates apply to cases resolved and do not measure unreported harm, firm-level prevention, compensation adequacy, or consumer welfare.
observations.subgroup: Complaints about financial products and services received by the Financial Ombudsman Service and its small-business service.
observations.counterinterpretation: Lower volume could reflect resolution by firms, reduced problematic activity, a backlog cycle, or changes in the mix and readiness of referrals rather than weakened consumer voice.

denominator.unit: new complaints received by the Financial Ombudsman Service in 2025/26

professional_representative_share_2024_2.unit: percent of caseload brought by professional representatives

professional_representative_share_2025_2.unit: percent of caseload brought by professional representatives

withdrawn_abandoned_share_2024_25.unit: percent of complaints withdrawn or abandoned after coming to the service

withdrawn_abandoned_share_2025_26.unit: percent of complaints withdrawn or abandoned after coming to the service

mechanism.value: Changing the cost and quality threshold for professional representation can alter who reaches formal redress and which cases survive the process, making access design part of consumer power

observations.method: Financial Ombudsman Service comparison of caseload share and case withdrawal/abandonment before and after charges for professional representatives were introduced.
observations.uncertainty: The source reports changes contemporaneous with the fee policy but does not identify a causal effect, applicant composition, direct consumer costs, cases diverted elsewhere, or whether better-evidenced referrals improved outcomes.
observations.subgroup: Complaints brought by professional representatives versus other routes; cases withdrawn or abandoned after referral.
observations.counterinterpretation: The lower representative share may indicate filtering of weak or unready cases rather than reduced access; lower abandonment may indicate better preparation or a changed case mix.

denominator.unit: new complaints received by the Financial Ombudsman Service in 2025/26; product counts are subsets

hire_purchase_motor_complaints.unit: new complaints about hire purchase motor finance

hire_purchase_motor_complaints_2024_25.unit: new complaints about hire purchase motor finance in prior year

current_account_fraud_scams_complaints.unit: current-account complaints involving fraud and scams

credit_card_irresponsible_lending_compla.unit: credit-card complaints about perceived irresponsible or unaffordable lending

mechanism.value: Consumer recourse is concentrated in mobility finance, payment accounts, fraud, and affordability—domains where financial products can reshape household room and everyday access

observations.method: Financial Ombudsman Service product-level administrative complaint counts and categories for financial year 2025/26.
observations.uncertainty: Product complaint counts are not prevalence estimates and do not show monetary loss, remedy amount, repeat complaints, or whether complaints were resolved by firms before referral.
observations.subgroup: Consumers using motor finance, current accounts, credit cards, and related financial products.
observations.counterinterpretation: High complaint volume can reflect product scale, awareness of the ombudsman, concentrated redress campaigns, or easier referral rather than worse product quality alone.

related_sources.claim: The Financial Ombudsman Service publishes quarterly, half-yearly, and annual complaint data for ongoing follow-up.
The service's 2026/27 plans describe expected complaint demand, fraud/scam cases, and redress-system modernization context.

boundary: This record adds UK administrative evidence on financial complaints, uphold outcomes, professional representation, abandonment, product-level harm signals, and redress routing. It does not establish population-level financial harm, causal effects of representative fees, compensation adequacy, firm compliance, or durable consumer trust.
